Kawasaki Is Bringing a Motorcycle With Legs to EICMA, Plans to Really Make It From 2035
15 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
It's been more than a year since Japanese bike maker Kawasaki came out, during the Osaka Expo 2025, with a vehicle the likes of which the world had never seen before. Part motorcycle, because at its core that's what it is, part dog, because it looks like one, and part horse, because it can carry a human on its back, the so-called Corleo will be making its public debut in Europe next week.
A product of Kawasaki Heavy Industries, the Corleo will be shown by Kawasaki Motors Europe at the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show, which opens its doors in Milan, Italy, at the beginning of November.
In all fairness, show is a bit of a strong word, as the company won't be bringing on the floor of the Fiera Milano Rho an actual, working prototype, but a full-scale mock-up. That's a bit disappointing, true, then again, it's much better than the computer-generated video of the Corleo in action we got last spring.
But what is this thing, after all? Officially a Robotic Multi-legged Vehicle (RMV), the machine is described as a new type of personal mobility vehicle. It was engineered with legs instead of wheels, and it's supposed to take its riders to places that are not easily accessible, not even on the backs of off-road motorcycles. Like, say, climbing mountains.
Kawasaki never revealed what frame the design is imagined around, but it did say its heart is a 150cc hydrogen engine fed by a canister holding the precious substance mounted at the rear.
The electricity the engine generates is used, among other things, to move the design's four legs by pouring into drive units installed inside each of them. The Japanese have not provided any details of the actual capabilities of this system.
Ok, so robots such as this we've seen before, so nothing spectacular there. But the way the Corleo has been imagined to operate is something out of this world, as it involves a human mounting it and riding it as they would a horse.
In a nutshell, the design can be ridden and steered using rider weight-shift inputs sent into a series of steps and handlebars. To make sure the Corleo doesn't slip or trip and hurt its rider, each of its legs is equipped with left-right divided rubber hooves.
Along with the announcement that the Corleo is coming to EICMA 2026 , Kawasaki also shared a few more details about the design, many of which have been kept under wraps until now. For instance, we learned that a special navigation system will be developed for it.
The goal of this system is to factor in all available data on weather, temperature, surface conditions, and even the presence of wildlife, so that riders can be guided on safe routes while in the wild.
This route will be displayed on the instrument panel we already knew the contraption comes with, which also shows hydrogen levels, directions, and rider position. Additionally, the navigation solution will also be available on various undisclosed smart devices.
Back when it was first announced, the Corleo, which also went by the name Concept 01, was just an insane idea, and there were no actual plans to produce it. That has changed in the meantime, and Kawasaki now says it will go for full commercialization by the middle of next decade.
